newsitem.title: USA: Oregon Treasurer meets with Moody's about reforms.
newsitem.headline: Oregon Treasurer meets with Moody's about reforms.

text.p: Oregon state Treasurer Jim Hill met bond rating agency officials to discuss a proposal to reform to the state's initiative process, a spokesman for the treasurer said Wednesday.

"The bond rating agencies are very concerned about the initiative process because of its uncertainty and because many initiatives have unintended consequences that put a financial strain on the state's finances," Hill said in a statement after meeting executives of Moody's Investors Service Inc.
Hill said he would support proposed legislation by Oregon House Speaker Lynn Lundquist to create a committee to review initiatives, hold hearings and issue financial impact reports on the measures.

The so-called Citizen Initiative Review Committee would consist of 12 members -- four appointed by the governor, four appointed by the president of the Senate and four appointed by the speaker of the House.
The report issued by the committee would not be binding on initiative sponsors.
"This review process keeps the measure's sponsors in full control and does not diminish the power of the initiative process in any way," Lundquist, a Republican, said.

"It simply aims to get objective information out to the public," Lundquist said. "I believe the voters want to know if a ballot measure may be unconstitutional or if it has a fiscal impact that could affect their tax burden."
Hill spokesman Michael Parker said Lundquist's proposal could allay some of the concerns of the rating agencies, and make it easier for Oregon to maintain and possibly raise its credit ratings.
